Let $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, let $U_0$ be unitary, and set $H_0=U_0^*AU_0$. For $j=1,\ldots,m$, suppose

$$H_j=P_j^*(H_{j-1}+E_j+D_j)P_j,$$

where each $P_j$ is unitary, $E_j$ is a local arithmetic perturbation, and $D_j$ is a local deflation perturbation. Then for $U_m=U_0P_1\cdots P_m$ there is a matrix $\Delta$ such that

$$H_m=U_m^*(A+\Delta)U_m,\qquad \|\Delta\|_F\le\sum_{j=1}^m\bigl(\|E_j\|_F+\|D_j\|_F\bigr).$$

The assertion also holds over $\mathbb R$ with orthogonal factors.

Let $F$ be a field, let $m,n,p\in\mathbb N$, and let
$A=(a_{ij})\in M_{m\times n}(F)$ and
$B=(b_{jk})\in M_{n\times p}(F)$. Their **matrix product** is the matrix
$AB\in M_{m\times p}(F)$ whose entries are

$$(AB)_{ik}:=\sum_{j\in n}a_{ij}b_{jk}.$$

The sum is the finite sum in the additive commutative monoid of $F$. If $n=0$,
it is the empty sum, so $AB$ is the zero matrix of shape $m$ by $p$.

The **identity matrix** $I_n\in M_n(F)$ has entry $1$ when $i=j$ and entry $0$
when $i\ne j$. In particular, $I_0$ is the unique empty matrix in $M_0(F)$.

Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, let $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$ and let
$A=(a_{ij})\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$. The **Frobenius norm** of $A$ is

$$\lVert A\rVert_F\;:=\;\Bigl(\,\sum_{i<m}\sum_{j<n}|a_{ij}|^{2}\Bigr)^{1/2},$$

where $|\cdot|$ is the absolute value on $\mathbb R$
([[def-abs-value]]) for $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ and the modulus on $\mathbb C$
([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]) for
$\mathbb F=\mathbb C$, and the outer power is the nonnegative real square root.

**The displayed quantity is a norm.** Regard $A$ as the element of the
coordinate space $\mathbb F^{mn}$ whose $j+in$-th entry is $a_{ij}$. The
standard coordinate inner product of [[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]
satisfies $\langle A,A\rangle=\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}\overline{a_{ij}}$, which equals
$\sum_{i,j}|a_{ij}|^{2}$ because $z\overline z=|z|^{2}$
([[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]]). Thus $\lVert A\rVert_F$ is
exactly the inner-product norm of [[def-inner-product-norm]] evaluated at $A$,
and the three norm axioms hold for $\lVert\cdot\rVert_F$ because they hold for
every inner-product norm. For real matrices the same sum is
$\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}^{2}$, since $|x|^{2}=x^{2}$ for real $x$ by the two cases of
[[def-abs-value]].

The Frobenius norm is the Euclidean norm of the full entry list, not the
largest factor by which the matrix stretches a single vector. It can coincide
with an induced $2$-norm in one-row or one-column cases, but in general it is a
different matrix norm from the induced operator norms used on this page. Its
relation to the spectral norm, its unitary invariance and its singular-value
formula are
[[thm-spectral-and-frobenius-norms-are-unitarily-invariant-with-singular-value-formulas-and-rank-comparison]].

Let $A=A^*$ and let $B=B^*$ be positive definite in
$\mathbb F^{n\times n}$, where $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.
If $B=LL^*$ is its Cholesky factorisation, then
$$C=L^{-1}AL^{-*}$$
is self-adjoint and has an orthonormal eigenbasis with real eigenvalues
$\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n$. The vectors
$$x_i=L^{-*}y_i\quad (i=1,\ldots,n)$$
form a basis satisfying $Ax_i=\lambda_iBx_i$ and
$x_i^*Bx_j=\delta_{ij}$. The generalized eigenvalues of $(A,B)$ are exactly
$[\lambda_i:1]$; none is infinite.

Let $n\ge1$, let $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let
$A,B\in\mathbb F^{n\times n}$ be Hermitian with $B$ positive definite. For
$x\in\mathbb F^n\setminus\{0\}$ and $\mu\in\mathbb R$, put
$r=Ax-\mu Bx$. Then
$$\operatorname{dist}(\mu,\sigma(A,B)) \le \frac{\|r\|_{B^{-1}}}{\|x\|_B},$$
where $\sigma(A,B)$ is the finite generalized spectrum and
$\operatorname{dist}(\mu,S):=\min_{\lambda\in S}|\mu-\lambda|$. Equivalently, the
interval with centre $\mu$ and radius $\|r\|_{B^{-1}}/\|x\|_B$ contains at
least one generalized eigenvalue.

Let $n\ge1$, let $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let
$A,B\in\mathbb F^{n\times n}$. The **matrix pencil** determined by $(A,B)$ is
$A-\lambda B$. Its determinant polynomial is
$f(\lambda)=\det(A-\lambda B)$, with real coefficients viewed as complex
coefficients when $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$. The pencil is **regular** if $f$ is
not the zero polynomial; otherwise it is **singular**.

For $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb C$ not both zero, put
$$p(\alpha,\beta)=\det(\beta A-\alpha B).$$
A **homogeneous generalized eigenvalue pair** is an equivalence class of such
pairs satisfying $p(\alpha,\beta)=0$, where $(\alpha,\beta)$ and
$(c\alpha,c\beta)$ represent the same pair for every $c\in\mathbb C\setminus
\{0\}$. If $\beta\ne0$, the associated finite generalized eigenvalue is
$\lambda=\alpha/\beta$; if $\beta=0$, the pair is an infinite generalized
eigenvalue. The pair $(0,0)$ is never an eigenvalue pair.
Write $\sigma(A,B)$ for the set of finite ratios $\alpha/\beta$ among these
homogeneous eigenvalue pairs.

routine_steps.claim: The matrix $M$ is positive definite because $u^TMu=2u_1^2+u_2^2>0$ for $u\ne0$. Also $u^TKu=2u_1^2+2(u_1-u_2)^2+u_2^2>0$ for $u\ne0$. The determinant polynomial is $\det(K-\lambda M)=(4-2\lambda)(3-\lambda)-4 =2(\lambda-1)(\lambda-4),$ so the pencil is regular and its eigenvalues are $1,4$.

For $x_1=(1,1)^T$, $Kx_1=(2,1)^T=Mx_1$. For $x_2=(1,-2)^T$, $Kx_2=(8,-8)^T=4Mx_2$. Their mass inner product is $x_1^TMx_2=2-2=0$. Thus they are distinct generalized eigenmodes and are $M$-orthogonal; [F1] gives the general real-spectrum and orthogonal-basis conclusion for this pencil.

For $x=e_1$ and $\mu=2$, the residual is $r=Kx-\mu Mx=(0,-2)^T$. Hence $\|x\|_M=\sqrt2$ and, since $M^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(1/2,1)$, $\|r\|_{M^{-1}}=2$. The theorem [F2] therefore bounds the distance from $2$ to $\{1,4\}$ by $2/\sqrt2=\sqrt2$; indeed that distance is $1$.

Use the operationwise real/complex arithmetic model, with six-real-operation complex products and componentwise division by positive real scalars. A scaled norm of a nonzero complex vector first chooses the largest absolute real or imaginary component $s>0$, rounds every real component divided by $s$, sums their rounded squares sequentially, rounds the positive square root, and rounds multiplication by $s$. For a Householder active block $C=[x\;B]$, $x\in\mathbb C^r$, a zero $x$ copies the block with identity action. Otherwise compute $\widehat N$ by the scaled norm. If $x_1=0$ put $\widehat\phi=1$; otherwise compute its modulus $\widehat a$ by its own two-component scaled norm and divide its real and imaginary parts by $\widehat a$. Set $\widehat\alpha=-\operatorname{fl}(\widehat\phi\widehat N)$ using real-scalar component multiplication, and $v=\operatorname{fl}(x-\widehat\alpha e_1)$. Compute $w$ by sequential summation of all $2r$ rounded real component squares of $v$, and $\widehat\tau=\operatorname{fl}(2/w)$. Compute $d=\operatorname{fl}(v^*B)$, $p=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat\tau v)$, $Z=\operatorname{fl}(pd)$, and $\widehat B=\operatorname{fl}(B-Z)$. Return $C_+=[\widehat\alpha e_1\;\widehat B]$, writing exact zeros below the target diagonal, and store $v,\widehat\tau$. Its theoretical representative is $H(v)=I-2vv^*/(v^*v)$. For a separate block application omit the column overwrite. For a right step apply these instructions to the conjugate-transposed block and transpose back.

For a Givens target pair $(a,b)$, use the identity when $b=0$, including $(0,0)$. Otherwise choose $\lambda$ as the largest absolute real/imaginary component of $(a,b)$, round $z=a/\lambda$ and $w=b/\lambda$ componentwise, and compute $h$ as the norm of their four already scaled components. If $z\ne0$, compute $n_z$ as the norm of its two components, $\widehat\phi=\operatorname{fl}(z/n_z)$, $c=\operatorname{fl}(n_z/h)$ and $s=\operatorname{fl}(\operatorname{fl}(\widehat\phi\overline w)/h)$. If $z=0$, set $c=0$ and $s=\operatorname{fl}(\overline w/h)$. Store $T=\begin{pmatrix}c&s\\-\overline s&c\end{pmatrix}$ and apply it to the chosen two rows using two complex products and one rounded componentwise addition for each output entry. For an actual target column, set its intended annihilated entry to exact zero after the update. The initial shift-vector rotation is formed from the shift vector but applied to the matrix without zeroing an unrelated matrix entry. Right applications use the conjugate-transposed form. Its exact unitary representative is $Q=T/\sqrt{c^2+|s|^2}$; this normalization defines a mathematical representative and is not an additional rounded operation.

These are arithmetic realizations of the canonical Householder and Givens methods. Returned dense transformation accumulators may be rounded; the exact unitary products used in backward-error statements are represented by the stored local data. Use [[alg-scaled-complex-householder-and-givens-updates]] successfully, with $0<u<1$ and $(r-1)u<1$ for every Householder dimension $r$. For a nonzero Householder column define

For a Givens step define
$$a_2=\frac{1+u}{(1-u)^2}-1,\quad q=\max\left\{\left(\frac{1+u}{1-u}\right)^3-1,\frac{(1+a_2)(1+6u)(1+u)}{(1-u)^3}-1\right\},$$
